subject: Renewal quote: scaling path options & throughput SLA
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbus.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:17:00Z
Subject: Renewal window + mid-term add — utilization attached

Hi Markus,

Hope you’re well. Our Dedicated pool renewal is coming up on July 1. We currently run a 32-GPU A100 reserved pool and have been hitting sustained peak batches during M-F business hours. Attached is our utilization report for May.

Two asks as we look at renewal:
- We expect to add ~8 GPUs mid-term (targeting Sept) to support a new realtime pipeline. Can you confirm a clean path to top-up mid-term without service interruption?
- We need a 95th-percentile throughput SLA for our 100 qps baseline (p50/p95 latency targets were included in the attached report). If SLA is a hard lift, what credits would you provide if throughput drops?

Also, what pricing differences should we expect between: a straight top-up vs re-profiling to a larger committed pool vs multi-year commit? Budget cycle is tight so we may need to combine a top-up with a 12-month extension.

Attached: Nimbus_utilization_May2026.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

— Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform, Nimbus Analytics
elena.ruiz@nimbus.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-29T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + mid-term add — utilization attached

Elena — thanks for the utilization file and the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes, a mid-term top-up is doable with zero downtime; the difference is unit economics and the contractual treatment of the added capacity.

High-level options (numbers illustrative; full quote attached):
1) Top-up (add 8 GPUs mid-term)
   - Mechanics: keep existing commit, add 8 GPUs as a paid add-on starting on the date you specify; pricing = monthly per-GPU rate (no reduction to original committed rate).
   - Upside: fast, minimal paperwork.
   - Pricing: add-on rate = $6,200/GPU/month (example).
2) Reprofile to larger reserved pool (retroactive reprice across committed capacity)
   - Mechanics: convert existing 32 into a 40-GPU commit with a new blended unit price.
   - Upside: lower unit price across the whole pool (we can offer an illustrative 8-12% blended discount vs add-on).
   - Downside: requires amending contract and a short reconciliation.
3) Multi-year extension + staged delivery
   - Mechanics: commit to 12–24 months with staged delivery of +8 GPUs in month 3.
   - Upside: deeper discounts (8–15% depending on term and payment terms).

Throughput SLA / credits: we provide a throughput SLO with financial credits capped at X% of monthly invoice for qualifying incidents. Typical credit structure: 5% monthly credit for sustained missed p95 windows, escalated tooling runbook, and optional on-call priority. We can tighten the SLO in exchange for a commensurate price uplift or an increase to committed capacity.

I attached a first-pass renewal_quote_NIM-2026-042-v1.pdf with the three price paths and sample math for your May utilization. Can you confirm which path you prefer and whether you want us to model a 12-month extension with the mid-term top-up?

If useful, we can schedule a 30-min call next week to walk pricing.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai

Attachments: renewal_quote_NIM-2026-042-v1.pdf (PDF, 58 KB)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T15:22:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: approval ask — NIM-2026-042 discount posture

Quick internal note — please keep internal. Elena has asked for aggressive economics if we want to close by their June procurement window. Proposed pricing posture for discussion:
- Offer A (top-up + 12m extension): 10% one-time credit on total remaining term if they sign within 21 days.
- Offer B (reprofile to 40 GPUs): 12% blended discount on unit price across all GPUs; requires amendment; legal review.
- Offer C (multi-year, 24m): 14% discount + upfront commit credit for prepayment.

SLA attachments: recommend we limit financial exposure to 5% cap per month and require runbook compliance for credits. Monica — can you validate margins on Offer B (reprofile) and confirm whether we can stretch to 14% on a 24-month?

Karthik
Director, Sales — Enterprise

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbus.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-06-05T10:09:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + mid-term add — utilization attached

Thanks Markus — helpful framing. A few clarifications and requests from our procurement team:
- We need a stronger throughput guarantee: p95 token latency <= 150ms at 100 qps. If missed, procurement wants a minimum 10% credit on the affected month.
- We’d prefer Offer A (top-up) because procurement can’t commit to a long reprofile workflow. If you can do top-up + 12 months and a 20% discount for the incremental 8 GPUs, we can likely sign quickly.
- Please confirm that adding 8 GPUs in Sept will not require migration or downtime for our production inference clusters.

Budget note: our headcount ramp was delayed so the deal economics matter. Happy to do a final review if you can send an updated quote reflecting top-up pricing with the 20% ask.

— Elena

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-12T08:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + mid-term add — utilization attached

Elena — appreciate the clarity. We can do a pragmatic counter that balances your procurement timing and our margin guardrails. New proposal (top-up + 12m extension):

- Mid-term top-up: +8 A100 GPUs effective 2026-09-01. Provisioning: non-disruptive; runtime supports hot-add, KV cache warmup expected 30–60 minutes for steady-state.
- Pricing: incremental 8 GPUs at $6,200/GPU/month gross.
- Discounting: one-time credit equal to 10% of the incremental 8-GPU charges applied to the first invoice post-provisioning (this mirrors a 10% discount on the add-on).
- SLA: we can commit to p95 <= 150ms at your 100 qps baseline. If our monitoring shows an SLO breach for >72 continuous hours after remediation window, we will issue a 5% credit on the impacted month’s invoice (capped at 5% of that month). For anything more aggressive (10% credit), we'd need a higher firm commitment (longer term or partial prepayment).

If you prefer a deeper discount on the incremental capacity (20%), we can offer that only with a 24-month extension or a 30% prepayment of the added capacity.

Next steps: I’ll update the quote to reflect the top-up path with the 10% one-time credit and the SLA language above. If that’s acceptable, I’ll send an updated PDF and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

— Markus

From: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@nimbus.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimbus.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal window + mid-term add — utilization attached

Markus — thanks. We reviewed your counter internally. We can accept the top-up path with the 10% one-time credit and the SLA with a 5% monthly cap as you outlined, provided provisioning is non-disruptive. We’ll go back to procurement to get sign-off on the 12-month extension; timeline looks doable.

Please send the updated quote and DocuSign link and we’ll aim to sign within the week.

Carlos Mendes
VP, Infrastructure — Nimbus Analytics
